transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I've been hearing voices lately and I'm convinced that people are watching and monitoring me all the time. On top of that, I've had these bursts of intense energy where my mood swings all over the place.
During the times when you are not experiencing those bursts of intense energy or mood swings, do you still experience the voices and the feeling that you are being watched?

Yes, even when my mood and energy levels go back to normal, the voices and the feeling of being watched don't stop. It actually happened recently for about two weeks straight where my mood was completely fine, but those things were still happening.
Looking back at your history, have you ever experienced these hallucinations and paranoia for at least two weeks when you were not having any significant changes in your mood or energy levels?

Yes, I definitely have. There was a period last year where my mood and energy levels were completely normal and stable for about three weeks, but the voices and the feeling of being watched never went away. It was really strange to experience those things without any of the mood swings.
During the entire time you have been dealing with these voices and paranoia, have your mood swings been present for the majority of the total duration of your illness?

Yes, they definitely have. I've been dealing with these issues for about a year and eight months now, and those intense mood swings have been present for the majority of that time. It feels like they've dominated most of the period I've been sick.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports prominent psychotic symptoms (hallucinations and delusions) that persist in the absence of mood symptoms for at least two weeks, which fulfills the diagnostic criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder. Furthermore, the patient confirms that mood symptoms have been present for the majority of the total duration of the illness, which aligns with the Bipolar Type classification. Schizophrenia is now less likely because the mood symptoms have been present for the majority of the total duration of the illness.
